case_name: Pichai Alias Pichandi and others v State of Tamil Nadu
respondent:
State of Tamil Nadu
Supreme Court of India

23 November 2004
Cr.A. No. 335 of 2004
The Order of the Court was as follows:
1.  There are seven appellants who have impugned the judgment and order of the High Court of Judicature at Madras in Criminal Appeal No. 793 of 1995 dated 30-9-2003. Before the High Court there were eight appellants but out of them A-2 is said to have died before this appeal was preferred and therefore, we are concerned with seven appellants only. They were tried by the Sessions Judge, Tiruvannamalai in Sessions Case No. 33 of 1994. The learned Sessions Judge found A-1, A-2 (since deceased) and A-5 to A-8 guilty u/s. 302 read with S. 34 IPC and A-3 and A-4 guilty of the offence u/s. 302 read with S. 109 IPC. All of them were sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life. Their appeal was dismissed by the High Court by the impugned judgment and order.
2.  The incident giving rise to this appeal took place on 25-8-1993 at about 6.30 p.m
facts: The incident giving rise to this appeal took place on 25-8-1993 at about 6.30 p.m.
It appears that most of the issues on which the villagers had disputes were trivial and were not of very serious nature.
The case of the prosecution is that on the date of occurrence, the appellants came to Village Poosanipadithangal and accosted the deceased who was in his house.
According to the doctor (PW 11) who conducted the post-mortem examination, Injuries 4, 5 and 6 were external injuries while Injuries 7, 8 and 9 were the corresponding internal injuries.
The first question is whether the appellants shared a common intention to commit an offence and if so, what offence.
issues: Whether the appellants shared a common intention to commit an offence and if so, what offence
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution has not come out with a true version of the occurrence.
There are inconsistencies in the evidence of the eyewitnesses which render them unreliable.
The role ascribed to A-5 to A-8 is not proved inasmuch as no injuries have been found on the person of the deceased which could be attributed to the assault on the deceased by these appellants.
At best they had come to teach him a lesson.
A-1 cannot be held guilty u/s. 302 read with S. 34 IPC because he did not intend to cause the death of the deceased.
respondent_arguments: The appellants came armed with sticks and the facts disclose that the sticks carried by them were not so harmless as they were projected to be, because injuries caused to the deceased by A-1 and A-2 resulted in the fracture of the skull which led to his death.
A-1 and A-2 cannot be absolved of their liability u/s. 302 read with S. 34 IPC.
They have been rightly convicted with the aid of S. 109.
According to him they should also be held guilty of the offence u/s. 302 read with S. 109 IPC because they abetted the commission of the murder.
court_reasoning: We are satisfied that such of the appellants who participated in the assault shared the common intention of causing grievous hurt punishable u/s. 324 read with S. 34 IPC at the inception.
The utterances of A-1 also indicate that they intended to give him a good beating and nothing more.
We find substance in the submission of the counsel for the appellants that A-1 and A-2 hit on the head of the deceased almost simultaneously with such force as to fracture his skull.
holding: The conviction of A-1 u/s. 302 read with S. 34 IPC is upheld.
A-3 and A-4 are found guilty u/s. 324 read with S. 109 IPC and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for two years.
So far as appellants A-5 to A-8 are concerned, it appears that they did not take part in the assault at all and the allegations made against them are not established by the evidence on record.
